sections.title: A) NEGATIVE ADVERBIALS: NO · NONE · NOT

blocks.heading: NO = not any (determinante) → "ningún / ninguna"
blocks.rule: Regla: va SIEMPRE seguido inmediatamente de un sustantivo. No + incontable / contable plural (o singular). El verbo va en afirmativo.
examples: I **have no money**. (= I don't have any money)
I have **no friends**.
**No student** passed the test.

wrong.good: I have no money / I don't have any money. (sin doble negación)

blocks.heading: NO + comparativo / expresiones fijas
blocks.rule: No delante de un comparativo (no more, no better, no longer...) y en expresiones como there's no point, no way, no idea, o prohibiciones (No + V-ing).
examples: There are **no more** people living here.
She is **no better** at maths than her brother.
He **no longer** works here.
**No smoking**.
There's **no point** in arguing.
formulas: There's NO point / NO idea / NO way

blocks.heading: Más usos de NO / NOT (Complete Advanced)
blocks.rule: No + different (no different = igual). Not + adverbio / sustantivo / cuantificador: not surprisingly, not coffee, not all. Respuestas cortas: I'm afraid not / I hope not. ¡No, none y not NO van con verbos negativos ni con hardly!
examples: This week has been **no different**.
**Not surprisingly**, he failed his driving test.
I ordered tea, **not coffee**.
'Can you come?' '**I'm afraid not**.'

blocks.heading: NONE = not one / not any (pronombre) → "ninguno / ni uno"
blocks.rule: Regla: REEMPLAZA a un sustantivo, por eso NO va seguido de un sustantivo... a menos que uses OF. Puede ir solo, como respuesta corta o al final de la frase.
examples: We looked for tickets, but we **found none**.
Do you have any books? — **None.**
How many mistakes did you make? — **None at all**.
blocks.formula: NONE  (pronombre: va solo, sin sustantivo detrás)

wrong.good: There were no tickets left / There were none left.

blocks.heading: NONE OF + sustantivo plural / incontable / pronombre
blocks.rule: None of + the / my / these... + sustantivo, o None of + us / you / them.
examples: **None of my friends** live in Sevilla.
**None of the information is** correct.
**None of us** knew the answer.
blocks.formula: NONE OF + the / my / these + sustantivo · NONE OF + us / them

compare.label: Plural → singular (formal) o plural
compare.text: **None of my friends lives / live** in Seville.

blocks.heading: NOT = adverbio → niega verbos (y adjetivos / adverbios)
blocks.rule: Regla: not niega verbos, normalmente con auxiliar (do not, is not, have not...). También niega adjetivos, adverbios y cuantificadores.
examples: I **do not agree**.
It's **not easy**.
I'm **not sure**.
blocks.formula: AUX + NOT + verbo · NOT + adj / adv

blocks.heading: NOT + cuantificadores / adverbios
blocks.rule: Not many, not much, not all, not everyone, not a single, not often... Aquí NO podemos usar no ni none.
examples: **Not many students** passed the test.
**Not everyone** agrees with you.
**Not a single person** came.
blocks.formula: NOT + many / much / all / everyone / a single

blocks.heading: NOT en inversiones y cleft sentences (C1)
blocks.rule: Not only + auxiliar + sujeto ..., but (sujeto) also ... · Not until + tiempo / oración + auxiliar + sujeto. Cleft: It was not until ... that ...
examples: **Not only did she win** the race, **but she also** broke the record.
**Not only is he** clever, **but he is also** kind.
**Not until I got home did I realise** I'd lost my wallet.
**It was not until midnight that** he arrived.
formulas: NOT ONLY + AUX + SUJETO ..., but (sujeto) also ...
NOT UNTIL + tiempo / oración + AUX + SUJETO

sections.subtitle: No va con sustantivos · None los sustituye · Not niega verbos

sections.title: B) PASSIVE VOICE

blocks.heading: ¿Qué es y cómo se forma?
blocks.rule: Pone el foco en la situación / acción, no en quién la hace. Necesitamos un verbo TRANSITIVO (con objeto directo). El O.D. pasa a ser sujeto + verbo TO BE en el tiempo de la frase original + PARTICIPIO (+ by + agente, solo si importa).
examples: Michael has studied climate change. → Climate change **has been studied by Michael**.
blocks.formula: OBJETO → SUJETO + TO BE (tiempo original) + PARTICIPIO + (by + agente)

wrong.bad: The accident was happened at 9 p.m.
wrong.good: The accident happened at 9 p.m. (happen es intransitivo: no hay pasiva)

blocks.heading: Tabla: la pasiva en todos los tiempos
blocks.rule: Truco: mira el tiempo del verbo activo y ponlo en TO BE. El verbo principal siempre va en participio. Ojo: el present / past perfect continuous y el future continuous NO tienen pasiva.

rows: I have been making a cake
I had been making a cake
I will have made a cake
A cake will have been made
I am going to make a cake
A cake is going to be made
I should have made a cake
A cake should have been made

blocks.heading: Verbos con dos objetos (give, send, offer, show, tell...)
blocks.rule: Lo más natural es que la PERSONA sea el sujeto de la pasiva.
examples: They gave me a prize. → **I was given a prize**.
Someone showed us the way. → **We were shown the way**.

blocks.heading: Infinitivo y gerundio pasivos
blocks.rule: to be + participio / being + participio, después de verbos que piden infinitivo o gerundio.
examples: She expects **to be invited**.
I hate **being told** what to do.

blocks.heading: ¿Cuándo usamos la pasiva? (Complete Advanced)
blocks.rule: Cuando el agente es desconocido, poco importante u obvio · en estilo formal o científico · para describir procesos · para dar 'flow' al texto: poner la información conocida al principio y evitar sujetos muy largos.
examples: My office **was broken into** last night.
He **was arrested** and **charged** with theft.
Water **was added** and the mixture **was heated** to 85°C.
The club management **was addressed** by the player who has won 'footballer of the year' most times.

sections.subtitle: El objeto pasa a sujeto: TO BE + participio

sections.title: C) PASSIVE WITH REPORTING VERBS

blocks.heading: Los reporting verbs
blocks.rule: Cuando aparecen estos verbos hay DOS formas de hacer la pasiva: la impersonal (It ... that) y la personal (Sujeto ... to + inf).
examples: Active: People **think that** young people drink a lot.

blocks.heading: 1. Pasiva IMPERSONAL: It + be + participio + that + oración
blocks.rule: Empieza por It. La segunda oración NO cambia: se copia tal cual.
examples: **It is thought that** young people drink a lot.
**It was said that** young people drank a lot.
blocks.formula: IT + IS / WAS + participio + THAT + oración (sin cambios)

blocks.heading: 2. Pasiva PERSONAL: Sujeto + be + participio + TO + infinitivo
blocks.rule: El sujeto de la segunda oración pasa al principio. El verbo de esa oración se convierte en un INFINITIVO, y la forma del infinitivo depende del tiempo (ver tabla).
examples: Young people **are thought to drink** a lot.
blocks.formula: SUJETO + IS / WAS + participio + TO + infinitivo

blocks.heading: ¿Por qué cambia el infinitivo? La clave
blocks.rule: El verbo de reporting (is thought / was said) ya marca CUÁNDO se opina. El infinitivo no tiene tiempos; solo indica si la acción ocurre AL MISMO TIEMPO que la opinión o ANTES. Mismo momento → to + inf (o to be + -ing si es continua). Momento anterior → infinitivo perfecto to have + participio (o to have been + -ing si es continua). Por eso el past simple, el present perfect y el past perfect van todos a to have + participio: los tres son "antes" del momento en que se opina.
examples: People think he lives in Paris. → He is thought **to live** in Paris. (presente – presente: mismo momento)
People think he lived in Paris. → He is thought **to have lived** in Paris. (presente – pasado: antes)
People thought he lived in Paris. → He was thought **to live** in Paris. (pasado – pasado: mismo momento)
People thought he had lived in Paris. → He was thought **to have lived** in Paris. (antes del pasado)
blocks.tip: Regla rápida: si los dos verbos van en el mismo tiempo (presente-presente o pasado-pasado) → to + inf. Si el verbo de reporting está en presente y el otro en pasado → to have + participio.

compare.label: MISMO momento
compare.text: → **to + inf** · **to be + -ing**  (He is thought **to live** in Paris)

compare.label: ANTES que la opinión
compare.text: → **to have + participio** · **to have been + -ing**  (He is thought **to have lived** in Paris)

blocks.heading: Tabla: People think that young people ... → Young people are thought ...
blocks.rule: Tiempo del verbo de la oración con THAT → forma del infinitivo en la pasiva personal.

headers: Tiempo en la oración con that
rows: Young people are thought to drink a lot.
Young people are expected to drink a lot.
Young people are thought to be drinking a lot.
Young people are thought to have drunk a lot.
Young people are thought to have drunk a lot.
Young people are thought to have drunk a lot.
Young people are thought to have been drinking a lot.
Present perfect cont. · have been drinking
Young people are thought to have been drinking a lot.
Past perfect cont. · had been drinking
Young people are thought to have been drinking a lot.

blocks.heading: Si la oración con that YA es pasiva
blocks.rule: Mismo momento → to be + participio. Antes → to have been + participio.
examples: We understand that the decision was made yesterday. → The decision is understood **to have been made** yesterday.
People believe the painting is kept in a vault. → The painting is believed **to be kept** in a vault.

blocks.heading: Negativa y sujetos plurales
blocks.rule: El NOT va justo delante del to. Police, people, cattle y clothes son plurales → are / were.
examples: They claim that the director didn't know about the scandal. → The director is claimed **not to have known** about the scandal.
The police **are believed to be looking** for more clues.
blocks.formula: SUJETO + be + participio + NOT + TO + inf

wrong.bad: The director is claimed to not have known.
wrong.good: The director is claimed not to have known.

wrong.bad: The police is looking for clues.
wrong.good: The police are looking for clues. (police = plural)

sections.subtitle: It is said that... / He is said to...

sections.title: D) PASSIVE WITH GET & PSEUDO PASSIVE (HAVE / GET SOMETHING DONE)

blocks.heading: Pasiva con GET (informal): get + participio
blocks.rule: Sustituye a be en la pasiva, sobre todo con cosas que nos pasan sin querer o de repente: get lost, get burnt, get stuck, get caught, get hurt, get fired, get married...
examples: We **got lost** in the forest.
Don't touch the oven or you'll **get burnt**.
We **got stuck** in traffic.
The thief **got caught** by a security guard.

blocks.heading: Pseudo passive: HAVE + objeto + PARTICIPIO
blocks.rule: Para decir que OTRA persona hace algo por nosotros (normalmente pagamos por ello). Get + objeto + participio es la alternativa informal.
examples: I am cutting my hair. (me lo corto yo) → **I am having my hair cut**. (me lo corta el peluquero)
I fixed my car. → **I had my car fixed**.
We print our photos. → **We have our photos printed**.

blocks.heading: Algo malo que nos pasa (experiencia)
blocks.rule: La misma estructura sirve para algo que alguien nos hace sin que lo queramos. ¡Sale mucho en transformaciones con break into (entrar a robar) y snatch (robar de un tirón)!
examples: Someone broke into our house. → We **had our house broken into**.
Someone snatched her bag. → She **had her bag snatched**.
My phone was stolen. → I **had my phone stolen**.

blocks.heading: Tabla: ¿en qué tiempo está? → HAVE va en ese tiempo, el verbo SIEMPRE en participio
blocks.rule: Mira el tiempo de la frase original: ese tiempo lo lleva HAVE (o GET). Luego el objeto, y al final el verbo principal en participio.

rows: I am having my hair cut
I have had the house painted
I was having the roof repaired
I had had the carpets cleaned
I will have the photos printed
I am going to service the car
I am going to have the car serviced
I must have my eyes checked

blocks.tip: Negativas y preguntas con do / did, porque have es verbo principal: Did you have your hair cut? · I didn't have my suit cleaned. "had had" (past perfect) NO es un error.
blocks.formula: HAVE (en el tiempo original) + OBJETO + PARTICIPIO

wrong.bad: Have you had your hair cut yesterday?
wrong.good: Did you have your hair cut yesterday?

wrong.bad: I had cut my hair at the hairdresser's.
wrong.good: I had my hair cut at the hairdresser's.

speaking.structure: It is often said that [statement], but I'm not entirely convinced that [opinion].
speaking.example: It is often said that technology isolates people, but I'm not entirely convinced that this is true.
speaking.translation: A menudo se dice que [afirmación], pero no estoy del todo convencido de que [opinión].

speaking.structure: Not only does [option] [verb], but it also [verb].
speaking.example: Not only does this option save money, but it also helps the environment.

speaking.structure: [Subject] is widely believed to [verb / have + participle], although [counter-argument].
speaking.example: Social media is widely believed to have changed the way we communicate, although not always for the better.

speaking.structure: None of these options is perfect, but if we had to choose one, [option] would be the most [adjective].
speaking.example: None of these options is perfect, but if we had to choose one, the second would be the most practical.
speaking.translation: Ninguna de estas opciones es perfecta, pero si tuviéramos que elegir una, [opción] sería la más [adjetivo].

speaking.structure: I usually have my [thing] [participle] at [place], although once I had my [thing] [participle].
speaking.example: I usually have my hair cut at a local barber's, although once I had my wallet stolen there!
speaking.translation: Normalmente me [verbo] el/la [cosa] en [lugar], aunque una vez me [verbo] el/la [cosa].
